reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a BSC/PancakeSwap front-running bot as an automated trading opportunity that allegedly produces profit from bid-and-ask differences after gas fees. It directs viewers to connect a wallet, send funds to a deployed contract, and use an automated action that allegedly returns 90% to the wallet. It also claims repeated daily use can produce earnings of up to a thousand BNB with more capital, although the records do not verify the code, profitability, transactions, or earnings.

citations.quote: if you just follow the description of the video as far as downloading MetaMask and also funding it Make sure that it's connected to the Binance Smart Chain
make sure that your wallet is connected to remix
So we're just going to send some funds to that contract we just created
we will just go over here and press the action button
It automatically buyers and sells for you

opening.argument: The presentation uses qualified language rather than an unconditional promise. Its example deducts gas fees from the proposed profit, and the speaker describes personal results as luck. The larger earnings figure is conditional on using more capital. Those qualifications leave room for trading costs and variable outcomes; they do not establish that every viewer will earn the amounts discussed. A judge should distinguish an optimistic account of a speculative trading method from a guaranteed-return offer.

citations.quote: The total profit of this front running transaction will be the difference between the bid and ask price (0.1 BNB) minus the higher gas fee, which is typically 0.03-0.05BNB.
I've had really good luck with this the last few weeks
you can have upwards of a thousand BnB a day if you use a large amount than what I started with

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument identifies wallet connection, funding, and an action button, but those steps alone do not prove deception. Its concern that earnings are unverified cuts both ways: the available material does not establish that the described transactions failed either. The speaker's discussion of gas costs and personal luck is more qualified than an unconditional profit guarantee.

citations.quote: So we're just going to send some funds to that contract we just created
minus the higher gas fee, which is typically 0.03-0.05BNB.
I've had really good luck with this the last few weeks

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Mentioning fees and luck is not a substantive warning about the risk to deposited funds. The speaker instructs viewers to fund the contract and activate it, then says it automatically trades and sends 90% back to the wallet. Conditional wording around the largest earnings claim does not verify the contract or offset the concrete expectation of returns.

citations.quote: So we're just going to send some funds to that contract we just created
It automatically buyers and sells for you.
It will automatically sell within a minute and from there it will take 90% and automatically transit back to your wallet.

opening.argument: The video presents a technical walkthrough: the speaker creates a contract in Remix, discusses the token and router addresses, connects a wallet, deploys, and checks the contract through BscScan. The sampled frames show the Solidity compiler and deployment workspace, not just a promotional claim. The speaker also says transaction reports could corroborate the stated gains. This is consistent with a demonstration of how the workflow operates; the existence of an earnings claim does not, by itself, erase the substantial programming and operational instruction.

citations.quote: we're going to be building our contract
now we have our deployment utility right here
which I can show the transaction reports on bsc scan to corroborate that

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument treats the funding and action steps as decisive, but they appear within a live contract walkthrough. The speaker describes checking that the deployed contract appears on BscScan before moving to funding. That sequence supports an operational-demonstration reading, even though the supplied material does not independently verify profitability. Lack of verification is a reason to withhold confidence in the earnings figure, not proof that the tutorial is deceptive.

citations.quote: now we have our deployment utility right here
we will just go over here and press the action button

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A technical interface does not change what viewers are being encouraged to do. The walkthrough proceeds from deployment to sending funds to the contract and pressing action, accompanied by claims that automated trades return money to the wallet. Saying reports could be shown is not the same as providing them; the cited demonstration does not verify the code's behavior or the claimed profits.

citations.quote: So we're just going to send some funds to that contract we just created
we will just go over here and press the action button
which I can show the transaction reports on bsc scan to corroborate that

opening.argument: The described activity is a software-enabled trading workflow using a wallet, a deployed contract, and PancakeSwap. The supplied material does not ask viewers for a seed phrase or password, and it describes no recruiting or downline income. Instead, the speaker presents a transaction mechanism and a stated allocation of proceeds between the wallet and protocol. Those details support reading the video as promotion of a trading tool or service. They do not establish that the tool works, but neither do they establish credential theft or a recruitment scheme.

citations.quote: How to acquire MetaMask Wallet: https://metamask.io/download.html
Remix Deploying https://remix.ethereum.org/
The remaining 10% will stay within the front running protocol.
Because, we're buying out on the same block of the liquidity.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument correctly notes that users are shown how to fund a contract, but a funded contract can also be the means of operating a trading tool. The record shows the speaker checking for a deployed address and describing a wallet-confirmed action; it does not independently establish that funds are diverted or that the stated trading operation is fictitious. The unverified earnings claim warrants skepticism, but it is not itself proof of a fraudulent mechanism.

citations.quote: We can, see that it's an address there now
So we're just going to send some funds to that contract we just created
to ask for another signature. So we confirm

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a seed-phrase request or downline does not answer the concern here. The speaker tells viewers to transfer funds to the contract, authorize an action, and expect automated trading proceeds to return to their wallet. That is a funded-contract profit proposition. Seeing an address and a wallet signature does not verify profitable trades or show that the contract will return the promised share.
